options.misconception: Johnson's position reflected détente with the Soviet Union.

options.text: Isolationism and withdrawal from all alliances

options.misconception: Johnson's position reflected the Good Neighbor Policy.
options.text: The Good Neighbor Policy toward Latin America

rationales.A: Détente with the Soviet Union was a later Nixon policy.
rationales.B: Johnson framed Vietnam as containment, stopping the spread of communism in Southeast Asia. His choice was to defend South Vietnam rather than abandon it to a communist takeover.
rationales.C: Isolationism and withdrawal are the opposite of Johnson's commitment.
rationales.D: The Good Neighbor Policy was a Latin America policy, not Vietnam.
rationales.general:
1. Read Johnson's choice. Help South Vietnam, or abandon it.
2. Name the policy. Containment: stopping the spread of communism.
3. Test the others. Détente came later; isolationism is the opposite; the Good Neighbor Policy was Latin America.
4. Match the framing. Helping an ally resist communism is containment in action.
Remember: name the Cold War policy — containment, détente, or withdrawal.

source: original; stimulus is a paraphrase of Lyndon B. Johnson’s addresses on Vietnam (1964–1965)
stem: Johnson’s position on Vietnam most directly reflected which of the following Cold War policies?

stimulus.source_note: Lyndon B. Johnson, address on Vietnam, 1964–1965, paraphrased from presidential addresses.
stimulus.text: We can continue to help the people of South Vietnam to defend their freedom or we can abandon them. I have chosen to continue our commitment to the freedom of South Vietnam.
